currentEarsLines.text: “SHALL” below states the requested behavior. All acceptance tests are specified, not executed by this design work. Cryptographic soundness and correspondence need arguments as well as tests. Performance targets remain unquantified until measurements support them; no arbitrary latency or proof-size promise is imposed.
| ID and class | Concrete SHALL proposal | Acceptance test/evidence | Present-support boundary |

| ZR01 — C, versioned interface | The native interface SHALL identify the exact ZKIR instruction semantics, compiler/lowerer, proof format, transcript, circuit/VK, SRS provenance, accumulator/decider format and ledger verifier versions required by an artifact. Unsupported combinations SHALL fail closed before financial acceptance. | Compatible tuple proves/verifies; change one version, transcript or serialization identifier and obtain explicit rejection. Retained artifacts verify in an independently installed compatible verifier. | Separate local pins and the historical contract/inner transcript mismatch are known; a comprehensive compatible release tuple is unknown. |

| ZR02 — C, general program relations | The interface SHALL support recursively composing proofs of developer-defined bounded relations expressible in the supported ZKIR profile, including both same-relation steps and explicitly compatible different-relation steps, without a maintainer program allowlist. | Independently author a new two-asset relation outside loan/swap fixtures; prove two steps. Compose compatible heterogeneous steps; reject a wrong relation with otherwise valid proof bytes. | MPS-0014 proposes same/cross-circuit composition. General Moriarty native capability is unestablished. |

| ZR03 — C, complete statement binding | Recursive verification SHALL bind canonical public inputs or binding commitments for program/semantics, property, signed intent, domain, predecessors, observations, complete effects, residual duties and resource limits; the application circuit SHALL enforce equality within the same canonical representation and pinned correspondence/refinement links where source, Core, ZKIR and ledger representations differ. Distinct representation hashes are expected; their authorized linkage is enforced. | Mutate each component individually while retaining other valid objects: every unauthorized mismatch of identity or its correspondence linkage rejects; mere inequality of different representation hashes is not a failure. Authorized witness variation and alternative permitted routes remain valid. | Ordinary proof input machinery exists, but this complete Moriarty statement and correspondence are open. |

| ZR04 — C, genesis and well-foundedness | A recursive compliance relation SHALL distinguish legitimate base cases from recursive cases and enforce well-founded descent or an equivalent sound induction structure; genesis funding, authority and initialization SHALL be authenticated. | Valid funded base and descendants verify; fabricated funded/approved genesis, recursive proof relabeled base, cycle and rank-wraparound reject. Require a soundness argument, not only finite tests. | An IVC example exists; application genesis and general sequence/DAG theorem are unestablished. A rank counter is one choice, not mandated syntax. |

| ZR05 — C, verifier identity | Every verified predecessor SHALL use a VK/relation identity authorized by the bound program policy, including any accumulator state and decider identity; a prover SHALL NOT select a weaker relation by substituting a key. | Proof of a trivial true circuit, wrong VK, wrong decider, stale compatible-looking module or substituted IVC state identity rejects. Explicitly authorized compatible module succeeds. | Historical PR738 described pinned inner-key hashes and a Collapsed-state hazard; current fix/deployment status unknown. Fixed keys and policy-checked dynamic keys are alternative realizations. |

| ZR06 — C, adversarial-witness soundness | For the supported profile, satisfaction of target constraints SHALL imply a valid semantic realization for every accepted witness, including type/range, Boolean, inactive-branch, encoding and output-shape premises. Honest-witness preprocessing SHALL NOT be the sole enforcement of such premises. | Prove the implication; challenge non-Boolean selectors/assertions, out-of-width comparisons, noncanonical encodings, unconstrained outputs and altered inactive-branch values where semantically material. Valid boundary values must remain accepted. | Explicit preconditions and constraint operations are visible locally. PR17's WShape premise remains conditional evidence, not blanket target soundness. |

| ZR07 — C, mandatory verification/control | The application relation SHALL ensure every mandatory predecessor and intention predicate constrains acceptance, including verification guards and all supported branches. An inactive verifier SHALL NOT satisfy an obligation for an active predecessor. | Set verification guard to zero, discard a computed false result, omit one required parent, or route through a failure branch that bypasses mandatory checks: reject. A deliberately optional inactive parent follows its specified semantics. | Historical PR738 allowed guard-based disabling. Safe application dominance and actual current lowering remain unestablished. This does not prohibit useful optional guards. |

| ZR08 — C, complete deferred verification | Before financial acceptance, the native verifier/ledger SHALL discharge every deferred cryptographic obligation necessary for the recursive statement, including all accumulators and final pairing/decider checks, binding them to the outer statement. No API SHALL report final validity after only the outer proof check when obligations remain. | Use a well-formed but invalid inner proof and a valid proof for the wrong instance that still permit outer proof construction; final verification rejects both. Dropped/substituted accumulators, semantic mismatches caused by reordering, and bypass paths reject; sound order-insensitive batching remains permitted. | Frozen September 11 evidence reports the accumulator pairing caught such cases in a PR test. Production/native general integration unknown. Separate or safely batched checks are both acceptable. |

| ZR09 — C, bounded multi-parent joins | The interface SHALL support a declared bounded number of predecessor proofs, at least two for MC06, and the application join relation SHALL enforce predecessor compatibility, resource partition/recombination, complete duties and aggregate budgets without double-counting common ancestry. The per-stage fan-in bound does not impose a single fixed global DAG depth; growing finite well-founded histories preserve declared episode/lifetime budgets through authorized continuation. | Split, advance two branches and join; reject duplicated spendable parent, missing branch duty, incompatible intent/domain, and cumulative-budget duplication. Harmless shared ancestry is accepted when correctly accounted. | General bounded joins and their full financial relation are open. Repeated verification instructions or a dedicated join primitive are alternative implementations. |

| ZR10 — C, state and ledger consumption | Native acceptance SHALL bind proved predecessor/resource identities to authenticated current ledger state and enforce the declared unique-consumption/nonce rules; imported certificates SHALL carry an authenticated anchor and cannot manufacture currentness. | Race two valid successors of one spendable state; at most one consumes it. Reject stale head, absent-head creation without authenticated absence, replay across domains and unrecognized anchor. | Historical ledger read validation is relevant evidence; the complete recursion/consumption integration is unestablished. Proof validity alone cannot provide this property. |

| ZR11 — C, compiler/effect correspondence | The compiler and accepted native statement SHALL preserve source stage results, rejection, exact arithmetic, effects and residual state, including guaranteed/fallible phase layout and every permitted retained-fee outcome. | Two-phase case with failed fallible business action: recorded guaranteed effects/fees match signed policy, nonce and duties. Unauthorized fee, missing liability or invented rollback rejects. Prove arbitrary-accepted-witness correspondence for the supported slice. | Source/5 and restricted Compact paths exist separately; full source/native/ledger relation is open. New ZKIR opcodes are not intrinsically required if existing constraints suffice. |

| ZR12 — C, public boundedness | Each admitted artifact SHALL have checked bounds for its stage computation, predecessor arity, public inputs, proof parsing, accumulators, memory-relevant structures and late-bound components under a pinned resource model. Exhaustion SHALL yield explicit rejection or a specified outcome without weakening mandatory verification. | Test each bound at maximum and one over; malicious lengths, excessive parents, huge proof encodings and budget-counter overflow reject predictably. Establish bound soundness independently of elapsed benchmark time. | Explicit bounded IR/source components exist; complete recursive-stage accounting remains unknown. Stage termination is not lifecycle liveness. |

| ZR13 — C/P, honest cost and feasibility reporting | Tooling SHALL report circuit rows/degree, proof/VK/PK and accumulator sizes, prover/verifier time and peak memory for the complete supported path; ledger costing SHALL account for deferred verification work. Performance objectives SHALL be stated separately and SHALL NOT permit skipped correctness checks. | Publish measurements across step depth, parent arity and heterogeneous relations with all final checks enabled, named hardware and versions; stress maximum supported shape and verify charged work coverage. | Historical measurements are useful machine-specific baselines. Future budgets/latency targets are not yet negotiated; no numeric target is asserted here. |

| ZR14 — C, private continuation interface | The recursive interface SHALL permit statements over binding private-state commitments with proved consistency, and tooling SHALL identify precisely which witness/proof/key artifacts a separately controlled successor needs. Claimed privacy SHALL name observers and leakage; proof reuse SHALL NOT be advertised as delivery of hidden state. | Separate Alice/Bob environments perform supported continuation and split/join without unauthorized secret access; missing witness data surfaces as unavailable, not a fabricated proof. Prove/assess declared confidentiality separately. | Native ZK is a foundation, not a private handoff theorem. MC06's separate-party witness and privacy obligations remain open. MPC is one possible provider with explicit assumptions, not a mandatory backend replacement. |

| ZR15 — C, semantic migration | A change to program, relation, VK, verifier or continuation schema SHALL preserve authenticated state, consumed resources, duties, recovery and disclosure constraints under the signed migration policy, or require applicable amendment authority. | Interface-compatible but semantically weaker upgrade rejects; authorized migration preserves consumed identities, outstanding debt and cumulative fees. Prior authorization cannot replay on a fresh domain accidentally. | Historical mutable deployment keys motivate this requirement. Full policy-preserving recursive migration is unknown. Immutable deployments are a valid initial implementation. |

| ZR16 — C, independent reproducibility and assurance | Native APIs SHALL distinguish compiled, synthesized, proved, outer-verified, fully verified and ledger-finalized evidence and expose retained proof/statement artifacts for independent final verification with pinned dependencies. | Independent verifier accepts retained valid two-step MC03 proof and MC06 split/join proof without original prover service; tampered statement/proof/key rejects. A simulation, mock proof or outer-only success never receives final-valid status. | Scoped proving examples and financial receipts exist; this end-to-end public developer evidence remains open. |

| MNR01 — Transcript and challenge specification | The qualified backend SHALL specify canonical transcript absorption order, domain tags, encodings, cross-field/limb conversion where non-native arithmetic is used, and challenge derivation, including verifier identity and recursive messages; circuit and native verifiers SHALL implement that same contract. | ZR01/03/06 | Compatible vectors agree; changed index digest, omitted challenge commitment, ambiguous encoding, invalid limbs and semantically changed parent ordering reject. | Pickles/Kimchi M05/M06; E10/E11/E15. |

| MNR02 — Deferred obligations, base cases and active masks | The interface SHALL identify each deferred obligation, authenticated inputs, producer, consumer and connecting invariant; final acceptance SHALL discharge every active obligation. Branch choice, predecessor cardinality, padding and base-case masks SHALL be constrained by the authorized relation. | ZR04/07/08/09/16 | Valid base and two-parent continuation pass. Changed deferred scalar/sponge, disabled required finalizer, empty required batch, recursive case relabeled base and dummy promoted to parent reject. | M01–M04/M07; E01–E09/E16; developer D01/D10. |

| MNR03 — Heterogeneous compatibility and key authorization | Each side-loaded relation SHALL bind statement schema, field order/encoding, child recursive shape, supported features, backend-specific proof-shape parameters (domain size and, where applicable, chunking or opening arity), key and parameter identity. Key data-to-identity integrity and identity-to-owner/program authorization SHALL both hold. | ZR01/02/05/09/12/13/15 | Compatible authorized heterogeneous relations pass; same-shaped trivial relation, misleading key hash, unauthorized key-root update, incompatible feature/field count and oversized domain reject. Distinguish child shape, direct fan-in and total ancestry. | M03/M06; developer D03–D05. |

| MNR04 — Verified values and auxiliary output | Tooling SHALL distinguish parsed proof data, cryptographically verified statements, witness-only or auxiliary values, predicted effects and authenticated actual effects. Every mandatory effect/history dependency SHALL be constrained and verified; current-state settlement SHALL include authoritative preconditions. | ZR03/07/10/11/16 | Invalid predecessor with consistent public fields, omitted verify call, altered auxiliary fee/recipient and valid stale-state proof cannot authorize effects. A verified permitted successor bound to current state passes. | Developer D01/D02/D06/D09/D10. |

| MNR05 — Production proof-mode separation | Evidence collection and deployed acceptance SHALL assert real proving and complete verification configuration; simulation, dummy proofs, disabled-proof mode and empty test keys SHALL be visibly distinct and SHALL NOT qualify production acceptance. | ZR01/07/16 | A local test-mode success with dummy proof fails an independent real verifier; mode toggles and mock ledger paths cannot yield a final-valid evidence record. | Developer D07; historical Midnight build-mode observations. |

| MNR06 — Parameter and cache provenance | Cache and parameter artifacts SHALL bind content digests, semantic/build tuple, purpose and expected identity. Batch parameters SHALL have a common authenticated identity or a proved compatibility relation; equal dimensions alone SHALL NOT establish compatibility. | ZR01/05/08/15/16 | Cold/warm builds preserve qualified semantics; stale/corrupt/relabeled cache entries reject or safely rebuild. Equal-length incompatible parameters reject or use an explicitly sound separate verification path. | M07; developer D08; no exploit claim from inspected TODO. |

| MNR07 — Batching and join soundness | Batching SHALL specify coefficient/challenge generation, full-batch binding, randomness assumptions, required cardinality and composed soundness error. Any bounded-fan-in tree decomposition SHALL preserve authorized parent coverage, duties and budgets. | ZR08/09/12/13 | A batch with one invalid member fails under its stated security guarantee; empty required batches, omitted member and adversarial cancellation/coefficient attempts fail. Binary-tree and permitted direct joins preserve the same financial relation; harmless shared ancestry is not duplicated spending. | M07/M08; developer D05. Tests do not replace probabilistic soundness arguments. |

| MNR08 — Specification and component assurance coverage | The qualification dossier SHALL trace mathematical statement, specification, compiler constraint and final verifier code for every used feature, and record exact audit/theorem scope and gaps for dependencies, custom gates, lookups, bindings and recursion. | ZR01/06/14/16 | A historical recursion-layer audit cannot qualify an unaudited gate or changed tuple. A complete supported-feature matrix names evidence or an open obligation for every component; documentation/code disagreement remains unresolved until reconciled. | 2023 Pickles audit extracted text pp3–8; visual check pp3/5/6; present study is not a new audit. |

currentEarsLines.text: After both fresh specification approvals, Grok SHALL implement import-safe `plugins/moriarty-dev/scripts/moriarty_dev/accounting.py`, called by existing `cli.py::cmd_run` for the exact `finalized-financial-settlement` profile. It SHALL provide preparation, current-projection validation and one-shot launch-claim operations within existing runner/store/record modules. It SHALL not create a new service, scheduler or alternate launcher. Tests SHALL use explicit isolated master, budget lock, projection, admission records and SQLite files including WAL/SHM; live stores/locks/registries and identity adoption remain untouched.

Input SHALL be the selected registered action, frozen hash-bound runner plan, canonical-store anchor and history reconciliation, contained current accounting reference, actual master path, exact reviewed resource amendment and both vote references, and current public observation references, discovered only through the authenticated resource-context requirement below. Output SHALL be either a named denial with no financial child, or a durable debit/current projection and a single matching plugin/master launch claim consumed by the existing guarded run. Missing or malformed authority/identity/projection input SHALL reject; tests may supply anchored fixture arguments, while live authority must come only from separately reviewed contained admission evidence. The separately declared read-only preflight allowance below is the sole exception allowing observation work before funding evidence exists.

The existing runner-plan validation SHALL be factored so preflight can verify exact executable/launcher/argv/action/candidate bytes before a debit exists. The single actual caller order is specified below; no final-admission-before-debit cycle or skip of final admission is allowed. Changed source after freeze needs both new source reviews and new current admission.

Within the same hash-bound resource amendment's existing `resources` object, `executionContext` SHALL contain exactly `path,sha256` for a contained immutable file. Its digest SHALL be committed by the immutable projection through a new required field `executionContextSha256`, so both projection resource votes also approve this context. The producer SHALL reject missing/disagreeing context digests; no argument, environment variable, CLI override or free-standing I2/SP01 reconciliation file supplies authority. `cli.py::cmd_run` SHALL resolve this context before constructing its live history reader and pass the positively validated anchor/history into existing store consumers. Ordinary non-live initialization/status/review SHALL not acquire authority or write tokens through this route.

The context SHALL contain exactly `schema,repository,gitCommonDir,store,history,observer,correspondencePath,expected,observerExecution`, with schema `moriarty.i2-execution-context/1`. Repository and gitCommonDir SHALL be canonical absolute identities for the authorized checkout/common directory, checked by the existing repository resolver. Store SHALL contain exactly `path,identityToken,inventory`, where path equals the canonical resolver's SQLite path and inventory is a contained immutable `{path,sha256}` reference to the pre-adoption inventory. The persisted in-store token SHALL exactly match identityToken. This declares a later reviewed adoption target; a missing token is unavailable, not permission to create it. Linked worktrees must resolve to the same authorized common store.

History SHALL be a contained immutable `{path,sha256}` reference. Its closed payload SHALL contain exactly `schema,repositoryKeys,requirement,capability,receipts,outcomes,eventBindings`, schema `moriarty.i2-retained-history/1`. RepositoryKeys is the exact reviewed list of historical checkout/common-directory keys to include, and requirement/capability are the current selected action's exact lineage. Receipts is a list of contained immutable `{path,sha256}` references to actual retained loan/related-operation outcomes. Each outcomes entry SHALL contain exactly `receiptSha256,defectClass,outcome,resolvedBy`, where outcome is exactly `failed`, `unknown` or `verified-success`, and resolvedBy is a list of explicit same-defect resolution receipt digests (empty means unresolved). Each eventBindings entry SHALL contain exactly `repository,requirement,capability,eventIds`, identifying already reconciled canonical-store rows. Verify those rows and receipt contents; unknown outcomes are not zero failures. Every referenced failed/unknown outcome must remain represented in history until an explicit applicable resolution is verified. Empty history/receipt/event mappings or mismatched checkout lineage deny the live action. Actual live reconciliation and token adoption are separately reviewed operations, not automatic initialization.

Observer SHALL contain exactly `entryPath,entrySha256,receiptPath,maxAgeSeconds,preflightSeconds,preflightAttempts,lockPath`. currentEarsLines.text: When a supported transaction spans several settlement steps, Moriarty SHALL represent each committed step and the outstanding transaction state explicitly.
- **THEN** The report and proof relation SHALL retain the unresolved stage and SHALL NOT claim full settlement.
When execution suspends for a later event, Moriarty SHALL persist a typed continuation bound to the program, predecessor, awaited events, authority and outstanding duties.
- **THEN** Continuation validation SHALL reject the replay or mismatched callback without consuming authority again.

When a submitted transaction specifies settlement conditions, Moriarty SHALL withhold the specified delivery until the required combination of authenticated signatures, documentary evidence, proofs, recipient actions and other supported predicates is satisfied.
- **THEN** Settlement validation SHALL reject release until the exact bound evidence combination is valid under its evaluation policy.
When a signed policy permits partial fulfillment, each accepted fill SHALL satisfy its fill rules and preserve cumulative bounds, remaining authority and residual obligations.
- **THEN** The verifier SHALL reject the fill or completion claim that violates cumulative bounds or drops the residual liability.
When a settlement step fails or remains unresolved, recovery SHALL distinguish a refund of still-controlled assets from a new compensating action after effects have committed.
- **THEN** Recovery validation SHALL reject the nonexistent inverse or duplicate refund and retain the actual committed history and outstanding duty.
When evidence resumes a stage, Moriarty SHALL authenticate its origin, correlation and declared finality, and enforce the specified consumption rule.
- **THEN** Evidence validation SHALL reject the unauthenticated or mismatched result and SHALL NOT use it to authorize financial effects.
When a program joins asynchronous branches, it SHALL specify availability and success policies separately and retain duties for unselected or late branches.
- **THEN** Join validation SHALL reject the missing obligation accounting; the losing or late branch SHALL remain accounted for.
When a stage executes, it SHALL use only the authority and consent granted for that stage under the signed lifecycle, revocation and expiry policy.
- **THEN** Authority validation SHALL reject the amplified permission or unauthorized destination amendment.
When execution spans stages, Moriarty SHALL account for cumulative costs, reserved resources and permitted retained fees under the signed bounds and target phase rules.
- **THEN** Resource validation SHALL reject the budget reset and preserve costs already incurred.
When a deadline or observation boundary is reached, Moriarty SHALL classify what is known and apply the signed expiry policy without treating missing evidence as proof of nonexecution.

- **THEN** Recovery validation SHALL reject a timeout-only claim of nonexecution and classify the relevant outcome according to available authenticated evidence, retaining unresolved duties where the evidence is insufficient.
When a suspended workflow resumes amid other activity, its proof SHALL preserve predecessor causality and revalidate the relevant state and authority under its signed policy.
- **THEN** The resuming stage SHALL reject stale evidence for changed relevant state or re-establish the required judgment under the signed policy.
When a tool simulates or reports a workflow, it SHALL state which stages, calls and proof judgments were covered and keep prediction separate from accepted execution.
- **THEN** The report SHALL expose the omitted execution or unproved judgment and SHALL NOT claim successful execution or proof.
Where evidence or workflow state is private, Moriarty SHALL define what each participant can observe and how later authorized stages obtain the witness needed to continue.
- **THEN** The privacy claim SHALL fail qualification when an observable output violates the declared disclosure relation.
When a staged program is compiled, correspondence SHALL preserve its permitted traces, conditions, rejection behavior and costs in the pinned Midnight ZKIRv3 execution model.
- **THEN** The compiler assurance report SHALL identify missing arbitrary-witness soundness; successful witness generation alone SHALL NOT certify the lowering.
When a developer composes supported constructs into a new workflow, validation SHALL use the versioned language and proof rules rather than a catalog of approved example programs.
- **THEN** The public toolchain SHALL NOT reject solely for missing project-registry membership when all required language, authorization, proof and ledger predicates hold.
When an application restricts participants or evidence issuers, Moriarty SHALL enforce its authenticated policy without imposing project approval on public program deployment.
- **THEN** The public validity relation SHALL ignore missing project or hosted-service receipts while still enforcing the signed application and participant policy.
When a stage is accepted, its authenticated effect frame SHALL account for exact assets and custody, authorized supply changes, fees and separately typed liability evolution.
- **THEN** The verifier SHALL reject dimensionally invalid equations or a settlement claim unsupported by the complete effect frame and external evidence.

When a participant authorizes a conditional workflow, the signing and reporting interface SHALL expose its canonical conditions, destination, evidence policy, allowed partial outcomes and recovery rules.
- **THEN** The signing/reporting conformance check SHALL reject the mismatch and expose the actual canonical recovery policy before authorization.

currentEarsLines.text: Certificate relations SHALL be Poseidon zk-stdlib relations verified through `VerifyProof` and `InnerProof` with guard constant 1, with each accumulator pairing checked by ledger `well_formed` on `ledger-10`. Contract-call proofs SHALL NOT be used as inner proofs. The outer relation SHALL constrain `vk_repr` and the state decider. Certificate campaigns SHALL NOT be admitted before a reviewed resource amendment, because the measured outer circuits need k = 18 for one level and k = 19 for two levels, above the Charter's k ≤ 17 ceiling.

Experiment E5 SHALL produce segment certificates over the Moriarty step at 1, 10 and 100 steps, with segment length at most 16 until benchmarked. Retained bytes SHALL be verified in a fresh process and imported through a certificate entry point.

Certificate campaigns SHALL NOT dispatch until each tracker item they need holds and is pinned: pull request 738 merged and `ledger-10` released, accumulator fee accounting, k ≥ 18 parameters served, released formats pinned and a reviewed resource amendment. The tracker SHALL also carry ledger 9 on Preview for `mandatory` and `composition`. If recursion slips, certificate stages SHALL record `blocked`, the core requirements and the Preview gate SHALL stand, and no scope SHALL be dropped without new user direction.

`Split` and `Join` within one contract SHALL be ledger-atomic. Child head identities SHALL be computed in the circuit. Budgets SHALL be conserved, obligations partitioned and authority attenuated. The lifetime invariant SHALL hold per head: `revision + remaining = allocatedLifetime(head)`, fixed when the head is created. `Join` SHALL require distinct heads and compatible policies. Fan-in and fan-out SHALL be at most 2 until the bounds freeze sets them.

Cross-contract `Release`, `JoinFrom` and `Reclaim` SHALL use claimed calls from the Compact 0.33 toolchain on ledger 9. An unclaimed `Release` applies alone and SHALL leave the head `Releasing`. `Reclaim` SHALL return a `Releasing` head to `Live` only when it claims, in the same intent, a target-side call that reads the release commitment as absent from the target's imported set and marks it dead there. Experiment E4 SHALL confirm this rule.

A successor SHALL prove from the head commitment and a recipient-encrypted opening, with no predecessor proof or witness. Per-party sub-state commitments SHALL be used where parties differ. Isolation evidence SHALL use distinct OS users or containers.

Sequential composition SHALL map to `Step`, disjoint parallel composition to `Split`, and atomic synchronization to same-contract `Join` or a claimed cross-contract call. Shared-state interleaving, asynchronous messaging and Pending SHALL receive a reviewed rule under head discipline before any SP10 campaign advertises them.

Moriarty acceptance SHALL count a contract-call proof as verified only when ledger `well_formed` checks it against the operation key read from `ContractState.operations`. A toolchain manifest SHALL pin Compact, ZKIR, ledger and proof-server versions for each network generation: ledger 8, ledger 9 and `ledger-10`.

Each Moriarty entry point SHALL compile to one circuit that proves authorization, transition validity, effect correspondence, intent refinement and the per-step invariant together. Every head write SHALL follow a read of that head in the same transcript section, with no checkpoint between them. Head creation SHALL follow an absence read. Every deployment used for acceptance evidence SHALL pass a deploy audit. The audit SHALL recompute the contract address and check the exact operation set, every key against a reproducible build, the initial state and the maintenance authority: committee `[]`, threshold ≥ 1, counter 0. The initial state SHALL be `Uninit(Π_P, netTag)` for a genesis deployment, or `Uninit(Π_P, netTag, A_pred)` for a migration successor, where `A_pred` equals the predecessor named in the signed migration digest. Final bounds SHALL come from the report's section 14.4 microbenchmarks on one pinned machine plus browser WASM measurements. The frozen set SHALL cover join fan-in, branch fan-out, certificates per call, segment length, effects, assets and obligations per step, public inputs per call, core step k, proving time and memory, and verifier work. Frozen bounds SHALL enter `bounds.json`, owned by MC01, and Π_P as a new program-digest version.

Acceptance SHALL discharge all four mandatory claim families at declared loci. ContractInvariant SHALL be discharged by the deploy-time property certificate and the per-step invariant. IntentRefinement and TransitionValidity SHALL be discharged by the fused step relation. HistoryCompliance SHALL be discharged by ledger applicability plus provenance: induction on ledger, or a certificate off ledger. One canonical claim vocabulary SHALL be used, with historical aliases recorded.

Deployment SHALL write `Uninit(Π_P, netTag)`. `Initialize` SHALL prove the genesis predicate with all-principal signatures, succeed at most once and derive `instanceId = H(A ‖ H(G))`. `Terminate` SHALL move a `Live` head to `Terminated` only under the contract rules' terminal condition or the principal threshold declared in Π_P, and SHALL record a disposition for every residual obligation.

Canonical encodings and test vectors SHALL exist for Π_P, intent digest v2 and genesis body v2. Exact-head mode SHALL bind netTag, contract, entry point, instance, head, revision, state commitment, Π_P, action and arguments, caps, observation policy, certificate requirements and validity window; its nonce is informational. Outcome mode SHALL bind the constraint set, a program-digest allowlist, the validity window and a nonce recorded in a per-instance consumed-nonce set. Π_P bounds SHALL be checked before proving.

Observations SHALL be signed by keys in `σ.oracleKeys` and verified in the step relation. The feed allowlist and `maxObservationAge` SHALL be part of the observation policy bound in the intent digest. Freshness SHALL use block-time reads in the transcript that the step relation proves and the ledger re-executes at application.

Operation keys SHALL be immutable. Replacement SHALL happen only through `Migrate` to a successor with a strictly greater version, under one of two branches. In the declared branch, Π_new SHALL be in the successor allowlist compiled into Π_old, which holds program digests only, and the migration threshold declared in Π_old SHALL sign netTag, A_old, A_new, Π_new, revision and state. In the unanimous branch, all principals SHALL sign `MORIARTY-MIGRATE-v2` over the same fields. The successor SHALL record its predecessor address in its deploy-time state `Uninit(Π_new, netTag, A_old)`. `ImportFrom` SHALL accept only a claimed `Migrate` call from that address whose commitment is absent from its imported set. An optional principal-threshold `Pause` entry point MAY halt new steps without changing keys. Cross-contract evidence requires ledger 9, and its Preview qualification is a tracked dependency.

**UISEC-001 Code identity and dispatch.** When a step dispatches a call, the interpreter SHALL execute only code whose identity is in the program code table bound by S. It SHALL reject any other identity.

**UISEC-002 Typed construction and matching.** When an ADT value is constructed or matched, the interpreter SHALL reject an undeclared tag, a wrong arity, a child of the wrong sort, a scalar presented as a reference, or a location that was never allocated. Matching SHALL be exhaustive or end in an explicit reject arm.
**UISEC-003 Acyclic immutable heap (D1).** While a value is live, its node SHALL remain unchanged. Each new node SHALL reference only locations below `nextLoc`.

**UISEC-004 Explicit frames.** When a call pushes a frame, `|K|` SHALL NOT exceed the declared `maxDepth`. A return SHALL pop exactly the frame on top, of the matching code identity and expected result type. Overflow SHALL yield an explicit `Exhausted` outcome.

**UISEC-005 Exact u128.** The interpreter SHALL compute every scalar result exactly in [0, 2¹²⁸−1]. Any intermediate overflow or underflow, or division by zero, SHALL reject with a named code. There is no wrap and no saturation. Rounding happens only under an explicit mode.

**UISEC-006 Step and total budget.** Before any effect of a step, the interpreter SHALL charge that step's declared cost. It SHALL reject when the cost exceeds `stepCap` or cumulative use exceeds `S.totalBudget`. Counters SHALL be checked against overflow and monotone across recursion. At joins, budget is partitioned and never duplicated.

**UISEC-007 Complete effects and residual duty.** When a step completes, exhausts or rejects, S SHALL carry the ordered complete effects and the full duty frame. Each liability SHALL satisfy `open + accrue − discharge = close`. No outcome, partial or failed, SHALL delete a duty. Refunds never reduce gross debit, and fees count against net.

**UISEC-008 Pending events.** While an external effect is unresolved, its unique event identity SHALL remain in P, in state Pending, Partial or Unknown. A timeout SHALL move it to Unknown, never to non-execution. Release SHALL require an authenticated non-execution observation. An event SHALL settle at most once.

**UISEC-009 Canonical step statement.** For each step or segment, S SHALL injectively bind program, semantics and code table; the pre- and post-digests of σ (heap root, `H(K)`, B, E, D, P); the step index; and the domain. Every field SHALL be labelled public, private or constant.
- genesis SHALL be an authenticated base case;
- every predecessor SHALL verify under an authorized relation identity;
- final acceptance SHALL run the decider, which checks every heap and state summary against its full data and discharges every deferred obligation (`midnight-ivc.md:103-116`);
- an outer-only success SHALL NOT be reported as final-valid.

**UISEC-011 Currentness is separate.** Where interpreter history verifies, the result SHALL NOT be reported as present entitlement until ledger state binding and unique consumption are observed. Of two valid successors, at most one SHALL consume.

**UISEC-012 Evidence-class labelling.** Every interpreter claim SHALL name its class from the table above, with tree, profile and premises. A Kore emission, a Quint sample or a K trace SHALL NOT be cited as correspondence, proof or ledger acceptance.

**Proposed behavior.** When a solver completes, combines or routes a partially specified signed intention, acceptance shall establish that the completed candidate refines every applicable signed constraint and permitted choice, binds all introduced effects and disclosures, and preserves existing commitments and residual duties. A completion outside that authorization requires a separately authorized amendment. Candidates remain uncommitted until ordinary acceptance succeeds; solver completion does not authorize rollback of earlier committed stages.

| APP-MOR-001 | When a new program uses supported constructs, the public toolchain shall apply objective semantic and proof checks without a project developer/program allowlist. | Clean developer environment with no workflow records; novel supported contract. |

| APP-MOR-002 | When an execution is accepted, its bound evidence shall establish both application invariants and the affected user's signed authority/outcome constraints. | Pool-invariant-valid trade with an unauthorized recipient rejects. |

| APP-MOR-003 | While an application is partially complete, it shall preserve outstanding liabilities, unconsumed authority and remaining work in successor state. | Partial redemption followed by restart cannot erase or duplicate the residual claim. |

| APP-MOR-004 | If a proposal changes its order identifier, acceptance shall not infer renewed economic authority from that change alone. | Two hashes cannot independently exhaust the same signed cumulative budget. |

| APP-MOR-005 | Where an oracle or solver ranks proposals, its output shall not substitute for the independently enforced validity predicate. | Malicious advice cannot make an invalid state transition pass. |

| APP-MOR-006 | When an application advertises privacy, it shall specify public disclosure and witness/communication assumptions separately from proof validity. | A delegated prover receiving plaintext is disclosed. |

| APP-MOR-007 | When an asynchronous remedy is described, the specification shall state its enabling conditions and required actor without treating an enabled transition as guaranteed submission. | Unavailable witness or absent submitter is not reported as finalized recovery. |

| APSS-PERM-001 | When a developer compiles or deploys a supported program, the toolchain shall not require a maintainer, reviewer, campaign or preferred-provider approval. | New developer deploys through a supported native route / valid candidate rejected solely for missing reviewer identity reveals violation. |

| APSS-PERM-002 | When an effect changes assets or liabilities, acceptance shall verify the applicable owner authority and program/intent constraints bound to that effect. | Authorized swap accepted / signature allowing spending is reused to create unauthorized debt and rejected. |

| APSS-PERM-003 | When a grant is signed or proved, its canonical binding shall include the interpretation version, domain, scope, recipient constraints, limits, lifetime and replay identity required by its profile. | Same decoded grant displayed and enforced / changed recipient, scale, domain or profile fails. |

| APSS-PERM-004 | When a delegate creates a child grant, acceptance shall establish that the child's allowed behaviors do not exceed the parent's and that required ancestry remains bound. | Smaller same-recipient allowance / child introduces new callback, liability right or larger grant and fails. |

| APSS-PERM-005 | When multiple uses share an aggregate allowance, accepted and reserved consumption shall be accounted for under one durable identity without exceeding the authorized total. | Two fills totaling 100 / concurrent 60+60 against limit 100 cannot both consume it. |

| APSS-PERM-006 | When replay, cancellation, expiry or revocation races with a fill, acceptance shall apply an explicit authoritative ordering and preserve already incurred obligations. | Confirmed revocation blocks later use / wallet logout alone cannot cancel a finalized obligation. |

| APSS-PERM-007 | When a permission is negotiated, the returned grant shall be distinguished from the request, and any increase shall require the root authority permitted by the profile. | Owner approves revised grant / delegated wallet response silently widens authority and fails. |

| APSS-PERM-008 | When external signing is requested, the request shall bind the authorized payload and key/domain derivation context; a returned signature shall not be reported as settled effects. | Authorized bound payload signed / same hash under wrong derivation policy or mere signature labeled settled fails. |

| APSS-PERM-009 | When viewing, proving, spending, policy-change or recovery rights are granted, each shall have a distinct documented scope and no unproved privilege conversion. | Auditor observes scoped data / viewing material accepted as spending authority fails. |

| APSS-PERM-010 | If required authority interpretation or currentness cannot be established within supported bounds, the effect acceptance path shall reject that attempted effect without substituting human developer approval. | Supported bounded policy evaluated / unknown permission type is ignored or routed to maintainer approval, violating the requirement. |

| APSS-PERM-011 | When a policy or account implementation changes, existing grants shall retain their signed interpretation or require explicitly authorized migration preserving liabilities and cumulative limits. | Compatible migration preserves remaining allowance / upgrade resets limit or adds method authority and fails. |

| APSS-PERM-012 | When a report claims authorization or privacy, it shall distinguish signature/threshold assumptions, current policy enforcement, tests, proofs and actual settled observations. | Report names evidence and observers / MPC signature alone represented as verified user intent or complete privacy fails. |

**EARS:** When a candidate plan requests any kernel-mediated external effect, the kernel shall establish that the exact effect and its material terms satisfy the applicable signed formal intention, and bind any proof, attestation and signing authorization used for acceptance to the same domain, stage, artifact/version and effect identity.

**EARS:** When membership, keys, attestation policy, verifier relation or adapter semantics changes, acceptance shall require the applicable signed evolution policy or amendment authority and shall preserve outstanding duties, recovery rights and replay scope across the change.

**EARS:** While any destination leg is unresolved or conditionally funded, the kernel shall retain its reservation and residual obligations, and shall authorize delivery, retry, refund or compensation only from authenticated adapter evidence and the signed stage policy, accounting for every already-final effect and applicable resource-uniqueness rule.
When a supported transaction spans several settlement steps, Moriarty shall represent each committed step and the outstanding transaction state explicitly.
When execution suspends for a later event, Moriarty shall persist a typed continuation bound to the program, predecessor, awaited events, authority and outstanding duties.

When a submitted transaction specifies settlement conditions, Moriarty shall withhold the specified delivery until the required combination of authenticated signatures, documentary evidence, proofs, recipient actions and other supported predicates is satisfied.
When a signed policy permits partial fulfillment, each accepted fill shall satisfy its fill rules and preserve cumulative bounds, remaining authority and residual obligations.
When a settlement step fails or remains unresolved, recovery shall distinguish a refund of still-controlled assets from a new compensating action after effects have committed.
When evidence resumes a stage, Moriarty shall authenticate its origin, correlation and declared finality, and enforce the specified consumption rule.
When a program joins asynchronous branches, it shall specify availability and success policies separately and retain duties for unselected or late branches.
When a stage executes, it shall use only the authority and consent granted for that stage under the signed lifecycle, revocation and expiry policy.
When execution spans stages, Moriarty shall account for cumulative costs, reserved resources and permitted retained fees under the signed bounds and target phase rules.
When a deadline or observation boundary is reached, Moriarty shall classify what is known and apply the signed expiry policy without treating missing evidence as proof of nonexecution.
When a suspended workflow resumes amid other activity, its proof shall preserve predecessor causality and revalidate the relevant state and authority under its signed policy.
When a tool simulates or reports a workflow, it shall state which stages, calls and proof judgments were covered and keep prediction separate from accepted execution.
Where evidence or workflow state is private, Moriarty shall define what each participant can observe and how later authorized stages obtain the witness needed to continue.
When a staged program is compiled, correspondence shall preserve its permitted traces, conditions, rejection behavior and costs in the pinned Midnight ZKIRv3 execution model.
When a developer composes supported constructs into a new workflow, validation shall use the versioned language and proof rules rather than a catalog of approved example programs.
When an application restricts participants or evidence issuers, Moriarty shall enforce its authenticated policy without imposing project approval on public program deployment.
When a stage is accepted, its authenticated effect frame shall account for exact assets and custody, authorized supply changes, fees and separately typed liability evolution.

When a participant authorizes a conditional workflow, the signing and reporting interface shall expose its canonical conditions, destination, evidence policy, allowed partial outcomes and recovery rules.

When a transition creates or increases a party's enforceable financial or operational obligation, it shall establish that party's consent to the obligation and its material terms, either directly or through an applicable prior authorization policy. A transfer to an address alone shall not manufacture such consent.

When a certified primitive substitutes for a reference expression, acceptance shall bind its version and establish preservation of reference semantics, preconditions, failure behavior and the relevant host/target correspondence.
Before accepting a stage under a bounded-execution claim, the verifier shall establish a resource bound for the concrete admitted artifact and any late-bound component under the bound cost model.

Acceptance shall bind program identity, semantic/profile version, signed intention, state and evidence according to their distinct commitment roles, and shall validate every permitted witness or program substitution against that binding.

Every declared mandatory intention predicate shall constrain transaction acceptance through a proved control/effect relation; computing or displaying a predicate without enforcing it shall not satisfy that requirement.

When a workflow claims atomic settlement, it shall identify the ledger/domain and the exact effects inside that atomic boundary; relocation and independent-chain effects shall retain separate pending and final states.
When gross obligations are netted, the transition shall preserve each authorized asset, party, fee, liability and residual duty under an explicit gross-to-net relation.

When a workflow invokes an interchangeable settlement implementation, acceptance shall establish its required financial and authority postconditions; matching an interface alone shall not discharge these obligations.

When an accepted transition relies on recursive history, its proof shall establish legitimate initial state, compatible predecessor statements and well-founded composition, including every consumed resource and residual obligation.

When code, verifier, policy or persistent continuation evolves, acceptance shall preserve the signed semantics, residual duties, recovery rights, privacy and resource constraints, or obtain applicable amendment authorization.

When a transition relies on absence, uniqueness or completeness, its proof shall bind an authenticated state domain and establish the required nonmembership or completeness property under explicit ledger assumptions.

When the kernel combines proofs, attestations and signing authority, it shall bind them to the same intention, domain, stage, epoch, artifact and exact effects, and expose the threshold, hardware, observation and recovery assumptions.
When a solver requests a financial effect, acceptance shall enforce the owner's bounded delegation across wallet, agent and signer boundaries.
When concurrent tasks or retries commit funds, acceptance shall reserve and account for spent, pending and residual amounts, including fees and sponsored execution.
When a service is purchased, the program shall distinguish payment finality, result availability and delivery to the authorized recipient, retaining each unresolved obligation.
When a request is retried or recovered, the workflow shall preserve one authenticated logical obligation and distinguish result retrieval from new billable work.

When a solver completes, combines or routes a partially specified authenticated intention, the language and acceptance relation shall establish that the completion refines every applicable signed constraint and permitted choice, binds all introduced effects and disclosures, and preserves existing commitments and residual duties. An out-of-scope change requires a separately authorized amendment. No developer or solver membership list may replace proof checking.

- **AR-E01:** When an intent is signed, Moriarty shall bind the program and semantics version, complete-effect policy, admissible partial outcomes, observation policy, authority, cumulative fee bound and recovery policy to the signed payload.

- **AR-E02:** When a stage commits an asynchronous effect, Moriarty shall persist its retained effects, reserved assets, liabilities and outstanding duties in the state authenticated by the transition proof.

- **AR-E03:** When a continuation executes, Moriarty shall validate its identity, predecessor or observation authority, prior-stage commitment, current duty state and single-use authorization before applying effects.
- **AR-E04:** When a stage fails, Moriarty shall prove the permitted failure transition including retained earlier effects, consumed authorization, fees, refund obligations and residual liabilities.
- **AR-E05:** When joined dependencies become available, Moriarty shall evaluate the complete dependency-result vector against the signed settlement policy before declaring settlement.
- **AR-E06:** While an external result is unresolved, Moriarty shall retain an unresolved duty and shall prevent timeout alone from being treated as proof of nonexecution.
- **AR-E07:** When refund, retry or compensation is attempted, Moriarty shall authorize and prove it as a separate transition whose failure preserves the remaining duty.

- **AR-E08:** When an outcome is reported as settled, Moriarty shall prove that all effect-relevant branches and duties satisfy the signed terminal policy, including any explicitly permitted residual obligations.
- **AR-E09:** When a stage incurs a fee or changes refund destination, Moriarty shall account for the per-stage payer, beneficiary, cost and cumulative budget in complete effects.

- **AR-E10:** When compiled ZKIRv3 execution is accepted, Moriarty shall bind the proof relation to the signed intent and certified source-to-target semantics, including the actual Midnight ledger phase boundary.

- **AR-E11:** Where a program meets objective language, proof and ledger validity conditions, Moriarty shall permit its deployment and use without maintainer, council, reviewer or hosted-solver approval.

- MPLR-031 — Delegated solver capabilities: acceptance shall enforce the owner's bounded delegation across wallet, agent and signer boundaries. Reject token possession as permission for arbitrary signing. Accept another unregistered solver using a valid capability.

- MPLR-032 — Concurrent service budgets: authorization shall reserve and account for spent, pending and residual amounts across concurrent tasks, retries and fee sponsorship. Reject two independently permitted purchases whose combined commitments exceed the budget.

- MPLR-033 — Payment and service completion: the program shall distinguish payment finality, result availability and delivery to the authorized recipient. Reject a payment receipt or TEE-vault result as proof of recipient delivery without the required evidence.

- MPLR-034 — Logical paid-request identity: retry and recovery shall preserve one authenticated logical obligation while distinguishing repeated result retrieval from new billable work. Reject duplicate spending or new service grants justified solely by replayed transport data.
